about: The chain prompts of the round-3 imagine-first A/B (ai/research/round3-plan.md §6, §8 D): the union of the chain requests in ai/experiments/imagine (c1, c2, g2, m5, n05, n08, n09, n10, n12, n13, n14: the ones its isChainRequest picks out of 40) and ai/experiments/search (c1, c2, g2, h01, h03, h04, h06, h07, h08, h14: its 'chain' cases), 18 unique. Same case format as cases/text.json (its groups and families; scored by score.mjs). expect.key is the index of the outcome that is the request's point (search's own; added for imagine's cases and m5, marked key_added): 'key outcome' in the bench report = that outcome holds in the final run. The per-stage checks are the plan's own (report.stages / report.goals of the build). origin: which experiment(s) the case comes from; chain: whether the client's isChainRequest (the imagine diff's regex) calls it a chain (auto makes a concept only then). Run: node ai/bench/run.mjs pipeline --set chains --imagine off|auto|always|observe|direct.

cases.prompt: Build a Rube Goldberg machine with at least four stages that ends with a ball dropping into a cup.

expect.rubric: At least four distinct stages, each clearly triggering the next (e.g. ball down a ramp -> dominoes -> seesaw or pendulum -> ball into the cup). The final ball really ends inside the cup in the run. Laid out left to right so it reads; no stage is decorative; nothing overlaps or floats unsupported (held items are fine).

cases.prompt: A marble rolls down two zig-zag ramps, knocks over a row of dominoes, and the last domino pushes a ball off a ledge into a bucket.

expect.rubric: Two ramps sloping opposite ways (a zig-zag: the marble runs down one, drops or turns onto the other), then a domino row, then a ball resting on a raised ledge (a block, book or box) at the end of the row, and a bucket below the ledge. The second ball only moves because the dominoes reach it, and it ends in the bucket.

Several different kinds of parts (dominoes, balls, ramps, levers, pendulums, springs…) triggering each other in a clear sequence from one start, left to right, with a satisfying ending. Every stage really fires in the run.

cases.prompt: Drop a basketball onto a trampoline so it bounces up and lands in a bucket.

expect.rubric: The basketball held well above the trampoline mat (slightly off-centre or angled so its bounce carries it sideways), a bucket beside the trampoline where the bounce comes down. The ball ends in the bucket (the bucket may be made wider; the basketball is 24 cm).

cases.prompt: A toy car races down a steep ramp, flies over a gap and lands on a second ramp.

expect.rubric: A steep first ramp with a toy car at its top, a clear gap, and a second ramp beyond it (a landing ramp). The car leaves the first ramp, flies over the gap through the air and comes down on the second ramp.

cases.prompt: Build a marble run: the marble zigzags down three ramps and drops into a bucket at the bottom.

expect.rubric: Three ramps stacked as a zig-zag (alternating slope directions, each one catching the marble from the one above), the marble starting at the top, running down all three in turn and finally dropping into a bucket.

cases.prompt: A pendulum knocks over a line of dominoes, and the last domino bumps a toy car so it rolls away down a ramp.

expect.rubric: A pendulum swings into the first domino of a row; the row falls in turn; the last domino nudges a toy car waiting at the top edge of a ramp, and the car rolls down the ramp. The car only moves because the dominoes reach it.

cases.prompt: desk chain reaction: a tennis ball rolls down a ruler propped on a book, knocks over a row of 6 dominoes, the last domino pushes a toy car, and the car crashes into a stack of plastic cups

may_missing.what: plastic cups that can be knocked over (the library's plastic cup is fixed in place)

expect.rubric: A ruler leaning from a book down to the table as a ramp with a tennis ball at its top; six dominoes in a row at its foot; a toy car right after the last domino; a stack of cups further on. The library's plastic cup is fixed in place, so a good answer says so honestly and stacks light stand-ins (foam blocks, small boxes) that the car can knock over, or uses fixed cups as the target and says they will not fall. Ball rolls, dominoes fall, the last pushes the car, the car hits the stack, in that order.

cases.prompt: Make a 5-step chain reaction: a steel ball rolls down a ramp, knocks over some dominoes, the last domino pushes a golf ball off a ledge onto a seesaw, and the seesaw flings a ping pong ball into a cup.

expect.rubric: Five stages in order: steel ball down a ramp -> domino row falls -> last domino pushes a golf ball off a raised ledge -> the golf ball lands on the raised end of a seesaw -> the seesaw flings a ping-pong ball, which lands in a cup. Each stage only fires because of the one before.

cases.prompt: For my physics class I need a 6-stage Rube Goldberg machine: a pendulum swings into a ball, the ball rolls down a ramp, it knocks over a row of dominoes, the last domino pushes a toy car down a second ramp, and the car smashes into a tower of 3 wooden blocks.

expect.rubric: Six stages left to right, each triggering the next: pendulum hits a ball; ball rolls down a ramp; ball knocks over a domino row; last domino pushes a toy car down a second ramp; the car hits a tower of exactly three stacked wooden blocks and knocks it down. Clear and readable for a class.

cases.prompt: kitchen table contraption with six steps: an orange rolls down a cutting board, hits a row of 5 dominoes, the last domino knocks a marble off a book, the marble rolls down a ruler, bumps a toy car, and the car rolls into a cereal box and knocks it over

expect.rubric: Six stages in order: orange rolls down a propped cutting board -> five dominoes fall -> the last knocks a marble off a book -> the marble rolls down a ruler ramp -> it bumps a toy car -> the car rolls into a standing cereal box and tips it over. Honest about anything the physics cannot do (e.g. a 5 g marble barely moving a car) and adapted so the chain still works.

cases.prompt: Build a 6-stage Rube Goldberg machine where each stage triggers the next, ending with a golf ball dropping into a cup.

expect.rubric: Six distinct stages (six different mechanisms or clearly separate steps), each one set off by the one before, laid out left to right, ending with the golf ball dropping into the cup. Every stage really fires in the run and the golf ball ends inside the cup.

cases.prompt: Make a spiral of 30 dominoes that ends by ringing a bell.

expect.rubric: The library has no bell and everything moves in one vertical plane (a spiral is not possible): both are said honestly, with a stand-in for the bell (something the last domino visibly hits). About 30 dominoes in a row (or rows) that all fall, and the last one hits the bell's stand-in.

cases.prompt: A pendulum swings down and knocks over a row of 15 dominoes; the last domino pushes a ball off a ledge and the ball falls into a bucket.

expect.rubric: Pendulum -> 15 dominoes -> a ball resting on a raised ledge at the end of the row -> the ball falls off the ledge into a bucket below. The ball only moves because the dominoes reach it, and it ends in the bucket.

cases.prompt: A steel ball rolls down a ramp and drops onto the high end of a seesaw, which launches a tennis ball from the other end into a basket.

expect.rubric: The steel ball comes down the ramp and lands on the seesaw's raised end; the tennis ball sitting on the low end is flung up and lands in the basket. The tennis ball must end inside the basket.

cases.prompt: Two pendulums side by side: the first swings into the second, and the second knocks a golf ball off a wooden block so it drops into a cup.

expect.rubric: Two pendulums; the first one released swings into the second, which then swings into the golf ball resting on a wooden block; the golf ball drops into a cup. The second pendulum must start at rest and only move because the first hits it.

cases.prompt: A conveyor belt carries a ball to its end, where the ball drops onto a ramp, rolls down it, and ends up in a bucket.

expect.rubric: The ball rides the belt, falls off its end onto a ramp below, rolls down the ramp and ends inside the bucket.

cases.prompt: Three rows of dominoes on three levels: the top row knocks a ball down onto the middle row, and the middle row knocks a ball down onto the bottom row, which all falls.

expect.rubric: Three domino rows at three heights (two on shelves); the top row sets off a ball that drops to the middle row, which sets off a ball that drops to the bottom row. Every row falls.
